media:group.media:title: Corrosion Analysis Lab (CoALab) | µfragtnach
media:group.media:description:
Korrosion verstehen: Was passiert, wenn Metall rostet? 🔬
Rost im Alltag ist nur eine Form von Korrosion. In dieser Folge von #µfragtnach schauen wir uns genauer an, wie dieser Prozess entsteht und wie er untersucht werden kann.
Gemeinsam mit Elisabeth Kolbinger, wissenschaftliche Mitarbeiterin am Fraunhofer IZM, besuchen wir das CoALab – auch liebevoll »CoALa« 🐨 genannt.
Im Labor erklärt Elisabeth:
▶️ wie sie Korrosion in künstlichem Meerwasser untersucht, ▶️ welche Analysemethoden dabei zum Einsatz kommen und ▶️ wie sich Korrosionsprozesse besser verstehen lassen.
Neugierig? Dann schaut jetzt rein und taucht ein in den Mikrokosmos des Fraunhofer IZM.
Ihr interessiert euch für Nachhaltigkeit und Zuverlässigkeit in der Elektronik und möchtet euch mit Expert*innen austauschen? Dann ist der Arbeitskreis »EcoReliability – Zuverlässige und nachhaltige Elektronik« vielleicht genau das Richtige für euch.
Das letzte Treffen dieses Jahres findet kommende Woche statt. Programm und Anmeldung: 👉 https://www.izm.fraunhofer.de/de/events/ak-ecorel.html

entry.title: Product Carbon Footprint: PCR & Standards for Electronics

media:group.media:title: Product Carbon Footprint: PCR & Standards for Electronics
media:group.media:description:
*Product Carbon Footprints need comparable and actionable data.* How can Product Carbon Footprint (PCF) data become reliable, actionable and comparable across the electronics value chain?
In this session, Dr. Chris Eckstein examines why greater harmonization and Product Category Rules (PCR) are needed for environmental assessments of electronic products and components.
Existing carbon footprint standards provide an important foundation, but they do not always offer sufficiently specific guidance for companies implementing concrete decarbonization measures. The presentation therefore explores current approaches to harmonizing PCF calculations and the methodological challenges that need to be addressed.
*Main Topics:* • Drivers for Product Carbon Footprints (PCF) • From Corporate to Product Carbon Footprints • Harmonization of PCF calculation methods • Current Method Development for Semiconductors and Data Center ICT • System Boundaries, Data Quality, and Modeling Rules • Component-specific PCF methods using printed circuit boards (PCBs) as an example
*Chapters:* 01:02 Demand, Drivers and Motivation for PCFs 15:31 PCF standards and guidelines 23:22 Ongoing methodology developments 39:48 Component level guidance: the example of PCB

entry.title: Greener Electronics: Ecodesign, Life Cycle Impacts & Competitiveness

media:group.media:title: Greener Electronics: Ecodesign, Life Cycle Impacts & Competitiveness
media:group.media:description:
*How can companies reduce the environmental impacts of electronics while strengthening competitiveness?*
In this Fraunhofer IZM expert session, Dr. Nils Nissen discusses how environmental performance can be considered together with cost, reliability, durability and regulatory requirements. Using examples from servers, routers, smartphones, semiconductor manufacturing and highly integrated electronics, the presentation shows why environmental optimization needs to consider the complete system and product life cycle rather than isolated components or measures.
Electronics are associated with environmental impacts across their entire life cycle. As electricity generation becomes less carbon-intensive in Germany, production-related impacts from globally distributed supply chains become increasingly relevant. At the same time, the most effective measures depend strongly on the product: energy efficiency can be decisive for continuously operated equipment, while materials, semiconductor manufacturing, transport, repairability and lifetime extension can become important for other types of electronics.
*Main Topics:* • Life Cycle Assessment & Carbon Footprint • Ecodesign & Environmental Hotspots • Energy, Materials & Manufacturing • Circularity & Product Lifetime • Semiconductors, Data & Competitiveness

entry.title: How Sustainable Are AI Data Centers? Energy, Water, Raw Materials & Life Cycle Assessment Explained

media:group.media:title: How Sustainable Are AI Data Centers? Energy, Water, Raw Materials & Life Cycle Assessment Explained
media:group.media:description:
*How sustainable are AI data centers? What impact do artificial intelligence, increasing computing power, and modern IT infrastructures have on energy consumption, water usage, and resource consumption?*
In this online expert session, Dr. Lutz Stobbe from Fraunhofer IZM provides in-depth insight into current developments surrounding data centers and AI data centers. The presentation highlights technical, economic, and environmental trends and demonstrates how the environmental impacts of digital infrastructures can be assessed using life cycle assessments and life cycle assessments.
Data centers form the backbone of the digital society. With the rapid growth of AI-based applications, the global demand for high-performance IT infrastructure is rising. At the same time, issues related to energy efficiency, resource conservation, and sustainable digitalization are becoming increasingly important.
*Key Topics:*
• The AI Boom: Developments, Market Trends, and Forecasts • Energy consumption of data centers and AI data centers • Water and raw material requirements of digital infrastructures • Life cycle assessment (LCA) methods • Life cycle assessment of a high-performance server • Environmental impacts of hardware manufacturing and operation • Eco-efficiency of data centers and IT systems • Prospects for a more sustainable digital infrastructure

The Laboratory for High-Frequency Microelectronics at Fraunhofer IZM supports companies throughout the development and qualification of advanced electronic systems. We analyze materials, characterize RF and high-frequency components, validate emerging technologies, and optimize the energy consumption of electronic systems from the earliest development stages.
From initial concepts and prototyping to technology qualification, our partners benefit from state-of-the-art laboratory infrastructure, scientific excellence, and extensive experience from research and industrial projects.

entry.title: 3D X-Ray Microscopy for Advanced Packaging and Chiplet Integration

media:group.media:title: 3D X-Ray Microscopy for Advanced Packaging and Chiplet Integration
media:group.media:description:
#BuildingAPECS I 4/4
As part of the ongoing expansion of the APECS Pilot Line, a new 3D X-ray microscope was installed at Fraunhofer IZM. Since the system was too heavy for the freight elevator, it had to be lifted by crane through a second-floor laboratory window.
The microscope enables high-resolution 3D imaging at the submicrometer scale. It expands capabilities for nondestructive analysis of packaging structures, interconnection technologies, and integrated microelectronic systems.
The system supports research in advanced packaging, chiplet integration, and system integration and strengthens the APECS Pilot Line as research infrastructure for advanced packaging and microelectronics.
Part 4 of 4 of the #BuildingAPECS series documenting the development of the APECS Pilot Line at Fraunhofer IZM.
As the APECS Pilot Line continues to take shape, it is creating research infrastructure for the next generation of microelectronics technologies. Our sincere thanks go to everyone involved in planning, procurement, logistics, cleanroom operations, and research whose dedication makes this effort possible.
About APECS
APECS (Advanced Packaging and Integration for Electronic Components and Systems) is a pilot line established under the EU Chips Act as part of the Chips for Europe Initiative. The pilot line strengthens Europe's capabilities in advanced packaging and heterogeneous system integration and supports the transition from research to industrial application.
APECS is coordinated by Fraunhofer and implemented together with the Research Fab Microelectronics Germany (FMD) and leading research organizations across Europe.
The project is funded through the Chips Joint Undertaking (supported by Horizon Europe and the Digital Europe Programme) and co-funded by national funding programs in several European countries.

media:group.media:description:
#BuildingAPECS I 3/4
A new high-precision bonder expands the APECS Pilot Line as research infrastructure for advanced packaging and microelectronics at Fraunhofer IZM.
Moving the system through doors, airlocks, and cleanroom areas required careful planning and precise coordination. Facilities staff, logistics specialists, machine owners, and the manufacturer worked closely together to bring the system safely to its final location.
The bonder expands research capabilities for high-precision interconnection technologies. It supports investigations in advanced packaging, chiplet integration, and system integration for future microelectronic systems.
